title: Lost in Translation: Large Language Models in Non-English Content Analysis

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing literature to evaluate performance disparities between high-resource (e.g., English) and low-resource languages, including analyzing the effects of training data scarcity, Anglocentric vocabulary tokenization, and the 'curse of multilinguality' in cross-lingual transfer.

Reviewing examples of machine translation and cross-lingual models forcing stereotyped gender associations when mapping pronouns from non-gendered languages (e.g., Hungarian) to gendered languages (e.g., English).

Referencing studies that demonstrate models generating violent language completions for certain religious groups (e.g., Muslims) and highlighting model failures to detect localized anti-Muslim hate speech contexts.
Citing existing literature that demonstrates large language models inferring negative sentiment from sentences containing disability-related terms.
